title: Few laborers (Matthew 9:27–38)
hookLine: he saw the crowds harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd
tomorrow: what can't you charge for, if you got it for free?

cards: A to-do list so long you stop reading it. A group project where one person ends up doing everything. Matthew's ninth chapter ends on that feeling, scaled up.
Two blind men follow Jesus down the road, shouting, "Thou son of David, have mercy on us." Inside a house he asks, "Believe ye that I am able to do this?" They see.
A man who couldn't speak starts talking, and the crowds marvel. And then Matthew pulls back to show what Jesus saw.

teach.b: Here's what he saw: "when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd." Worn out. Scattered.
Nobody tending them. It's the kind of sight that's easy to scroll past. Then he turns to his disciples and changes the picture: "The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few."
The same crowd that looked like lost sheep now looks like a field ready to bring in. The need hasn't shrunk; it's been seen another way. And the problem isn't the crop.
It's the shortage of hands. So what's the first move, when the need is huge? Not a strategy, not working harder.
A prayer, handed to his friends: "Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest." The field belongs to someone else.
The workers are asked for, not drafted.

teach.h: PRAY THE LORD OF THE HARVEST.
teach.b: And there's a turn waiting on the next page: the people told to pray for workers are about to be sent.
In Matthew, praying for help and becoming the help sit a breath apart.

how: Some Christians pray Matthew 9:38 for people entering ministry or service, and some churches set aside days to pray for vocations and for workers in hospitals, schools and missions.

games.q: the neighborhood food pantry posts: shelves full, volunteers few. you can't cover it alone. what's Matthew 9's first move?
o: ask for help: pray, and recruit one more pair of hands.

games.why: seeing a plenteous harvest and few labourers, Jesus' first move was to have his friends pray for workers, and then they were sent.

practice: Write one name on a scrap of paper: a person you'd want beside you for a job too big to do alone. If you pray, you can ask the Lord of the harvest to send that help; if you don't, let the name sit there as your first ask.

wordCard.voice: Few laborers. A field too big for the hands in it, and a first move that's a prayer.

orig.note: Greek: to be moved with compassion. Matthew 9:36 uses it of Jesus looking at the crowds.
